rationale: The only error is a page-level 'The form has errors' that never names which field failed, so the item in error is not identified.

rationale: ZIP is the empty required field, but the error names the valid Email field, so it identifies the wrong item as being in error.

rationale: The only error indication is a red border with no text, so the item in error is not identified or described in text.

rationale: With three named required fields, the error says only 'A required field is empty' and never identifies which field is in error.

rationale: The message does not repeat the label verbatim, but it is the single field, is bound via aria-describedby, and sits directly under the labelled control, so the item in error is identified.

rationale: The error summary names the failing 'Email' field and links to it, identifying the item in error in text.

rationale: Color is used redundantly with a text error that names the Email field, so color is not the only cue and the item in error is identified in text.

rationale: The error mirrors the Trusted Tester PASS pattern 'Error: Password field.' plus a description, identifying and describing the item in error in text.

rationale: The field's accessible name is supplied by aria-label ('Subscriber email') and the error names exactly that, correctly identifying the item in error.

rationale: The control has no programmatic accessible name (visible 'Party size' text is not associated), so whether the error's human phrasing correctly names this specific field cannot be deterministically resolved by name-matching; the runner should abstain rather than assert a name mismatch.
citation: "the item that is in error is identified ..." — WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.1 (without a programmatic name, name-correctness is not deterministically decidable)
